pl-l3d19c6-d1e114.summary: States that he alone is called mediator, not the Father or the Holy Spirit.
claims: Only the Son is called mediator.

pl-l3d19c6-d1e117.summary: Expounds 1 Tim 2:5, 'one mediator of God and men, the man Christ Jesus': through his humanity he stands in the middle as arbiter to make peace, reconciling men to God, the arbiter Job desired (Job 9:33). We are reconciled to God by Christ's death (Rom 5:10), not as if God began to love those he hated, as enemies are reconciled, but we were reconciled to a God who already loved us; he loved us before the world, before we existed. We were at enmity with him through sin while he had charity toward us; we were enemies to God as sins are enemies to justice, so when sins are remitted the enmity ends and those he justifies are reconciled to the just one.
claims: Reconciliation does not mean God began to love those he hated.
God loved us before the world.
Our enmity with God was that of sin to justice.

pl-l3d19c6-d1e142.summary: Explains that Christ is called mediator because, being between God and men, he reconciles them to God by taking away men's offenses from God's eyes, i.e., blotting out the sins that offended God and made us his enemies.
claims: Christ reconciles by blotting out the sins that offended God.

pl-l3d19c6-d1e145.summary: Raises a question: since not only the Son but the Father and Spirit blot out sins, and that blotting out is our reconciliation, why is only the Son called mediator? Of the Father it is said that God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself (2 Cor 5:19); since he reconciles, why is he not mediator?
claims: Objection: the Father also reconciles, so should be called mediator.

pl-l3d19c6-d1e152.summary: Answers that the Father is not between God and men, nor did he have in himself the mysteries by whose faith and imitation we are justified, i.e., reconciled to God. The whole Trinity reconciled us by use of power in blotting out sins, but the Son alone by fulfilling obedience, since in him, according to his human nature, were accomplished the things by which believers and imitators are justified.
claims: The whole Trinity reconciles by power.
Only the Son reconciles by obedience in his humanity.

pl-l3d19c6.summary: Explains why only the Son is called mediator, not the Father or Spirit. Christ is the arbiter Job desired (1 Tim 2:5), reconciling men to God by his death. This does not mean God began to love those he hated: he loved us before the world; we were his enemies as sins are enemies of justice, and when sins are remitted the enmity ends. Christ reconciles by removing from God's eyes the sins that offended him. Since the whole Trinity remits sins, and the Father reconciled the world to himself (2 Cor 5:19), why is only the Son mediator? Because the Father is not between God and men and did not have in himself the mysteries by whose faith and imitation we are justified. The whole Trinity reconciled us by use of power; the Son alone by fulfilling obedience in his human nature.
claims: Only the Son is called mediator.
Reconciliation does not mean God began to love those he hated.
God loved us before the world was.
Christ reconciles by removing the sins that offended God.
The whole Trinity reconciles by power; the Son alone by obedience in his humanity.
